learningObjectives.title: Textile artists and the formal elements

questions.q: In weaving, what is the name given to the set of threads held taut lengthways on the loom?
options: The weft
The warp
The selvedge
The pile
questions.explain: The warp threads run lengthways and are held under tension on the loom, while the weft is woven across them.

questions.q: In the batik technique, which material is used to resist the dye?
options: Hot wax
Bleach
Salt
Starch paste
questions.explain: In batik, hot wax is applied to areas of fabric so the dye cannot penetrate them, creating a pattern.

questions.q: Tie-dye is an example of which category of textile process?
options: Resist dyeing
Weaving
Felting
Embossing
questions.explain: Tie-dye binds or ties areas of cloth so the dye cannot reach them, making it a resist-dyeing method.

questions.q: What does the technique of appliqué involve?
options: Stitching or fixing cut fabric shapes onto a background fabric
Weaving threads at right angles on a loom
Matting wool fibres together with heat and water
Pressing dye through a mesh screen
questions.explain: Appliqué builds an image by attaching cut pieces of fabric onto a base cloth, usually by stitching.

questions.q: Which fibre is traditionally used to make felt?
options: Wool
Cotton
Silk
Polyester
questions.explain: Wool fibres have tiny scales that interlock under heat, moisture and agitation, allowing them to felt together.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the formal elements used to analyse textile work?
options: Texture
Warp
Mordant
Squeegee
questions.explain: Texture is a formal element and is especially important in textiles, alongside line, shape, form, tone, colour and pattern.

questions.q: The textile designer William Morris is most closely associated with which movement?
options: The Arts and Crafts movement
Pop Art
Cubism
Surrealism
questions.explain: William Morris was a leading figure of the Arts and Crafts movement, known for his printed and woven textile and wallpaper designs.

questions.q: Which tool is used to push ink through the mesh in screen printing?
options: A squeegee
A shuttle
A bobbin
A mordant
questions.explain: A squeegee is drawn across the screen to force ink through the open areas of the mesh onto the fabric below.

questions.q: Why is a mordant often used when dyeing fabric with natural dyes?
options: To help fix the dye to the fibres and improve colourfastness
To bleach the fabric before dyeing
To make the fabric waterproof
To soften the fabric after weaving
questions.explain: A mordant bonds the dye to the fibre so the colour is fixed and less likely to wash or fade out.

questions.q: How does the weft differ from the warp in a woven fabric?
options: The weft is threaded across, over and under the lengthways warp threads
The weft is stitched on top of the finished cloth
The weft is sprayed on as a dye
The weft is the wax applied in batik
questions.explain: The weft is woven horizontally across, passing over and under the tensioned warp threads to build the cloth.

questions.q: Why can wool be turned into felt but polyester generally cannot?
options: Wool fibres have scales that interlock when agitated, whereas smooth synthetic fibres do not
Wool is heavier than polyester so it sticks together
Polyester dissolves in warm water
Wool contains natural glue that polyester lacks
questions.explain: The microscopic scales on wool fibres tangle and lock together under heat, moisture and friction, which smooth synthetic fibres cannot do.

questions.q: What is the underlying principle shared by batik and tie-dye?
options: Parts of the fabric are protected so the dye cannot reach them
The fabric is woven from two different fibres
Colour is removed from a pre-dyed cloth
Fabric shapes are layered and stitched together
questions.explain: Both are resist techniques: wax in batik and binding in tie-dye block the dye from certain areas to form a pattern.

questions.q: Which formal element is being explored when an artist combines smooth silk with rough hessian and raised stitching?
options: Texture
Tone
Colour
Line
questions.explain: Contrasting smooth, rough and raised surfaces is a direct exploration of texture, the surface quality of a material.

questions.q: In relief block printing, why does the raised part of the block carry the design?
options: Ink sits on the raised surface and is pressed onto the fabric, while cut-away areas stay blank
The cut-away areas hold the ink and print the pattern
The whole block is dipped in dye and stamped
Ink is pushed through holes cut in the block
questions.explain: In relief printing the ink coats the raised areas, so only the uncut surface transfers the image to the fabric.

questions.q: What is one key difference between hand embroidery and machine embroidery?
options: Hand embroidery is stitched individually by hand, while machine embroidery uses a sewing machine to work faster and more repeatably
Hand embroidery uses no thread, unlike machine embroidery
Machine embroidery can only be done on paper
Hand embroidery cannot use coloured threads
questions.explain: Hand embroidery gives individual control over each stitch, whereas machine embroidery is quicker and better suited to repeated marks.

questions.q: What does discharge printing do to a fabric?
options: It removes or bleaches colour from an already-dyed fabric to create a pattern
It weaves two colours together on a loom
It seals wax onto the surface of the cloth
It stitches padding between two layers of fabric
questions.explain: Discharge printing applies a paste that takes colour out of a dyed cloth, producing a lighter design on a darker ground.

questions.q: A student wants to repeat the same motif many times evenly across a length of fabric. Which technique is best suited to this?
options: Block or screen printing
Single hand-stitched embroidery of each motif
Wet felting
Tie-dye
questions.explain: Block and screen printing use a reusable stamp or stencil, making it easy to repeat an identical motif consistently across the cloth.

questions.q: A student wants to add raised, three-dimensional surface texture to a flat piece of cloth. Which approach would achieve this most directly?
options: Layering appliqué with raised stitching
Flat screen printing in one colour
Soaking the fabric in a single dye bath
Ironing the fabric smooth
questions.explain: Building up fabric layers with appliqué and adding stitching creates physical, raised texture on the surface.

questions.q: A student researching William Morris wants their own outcome to reflect his approach. Which starting point best fits his work?
options: Designing a repeating pattern based on natural forms such as leaves and flowers
Creating a random splattered abstract with no repeat
Using only plain undyed calico with no pattern
Photographing machinery for an industrial theme
questions.explain: Morris's textiles are known for stylised repeating patterns drawn from nature, so plant-based repeats reflect his approach.

questions.q: A student is choosing a fabric to natural-dye so the colour holds well. Which choice is most suitable?
options: A natural fibre such as cotton or wool, treated with a mordant
A smooth synthetic such as polyester with no preparation
A pre-waxed batik cloth left fully covered in wax
A plastic-coated fabric
questions.explain: Natural fibres absorb natural dyes well, and a mordant fixes the colour so it is more colourfast.
